sources.summary: El País in English (14 Apr 2025) on the killing of Sara Millerey (32), a trans woman, in Bello, Antioquia: beaten and thrown into a creek, died of her injuries, onlookers filmed instead of helping; the third LGBTQ+ killing in Bello in 2025; 13 trans people killed nationally in Q1 2025. National context — no Quindío-specific content.

CNN (6 Aug 2025) follow-up in the 'As Equals' series: the viral Millerey video shocked the country but the killings continued — armed gangs; frames being queer in parts of the country as 'to sign your own death sentence'. National context.

The Guardian (30 Jul 2024): armed groups threatening a wave of 'social cleansing' against trans women in Caquetá — Tatiana Cespedes (51) given a week to leave or be killed, twice displaced; 41 trans women killed in the country in 2023, 8 killed Feb–Apr 2024; flyers list trans women as legitimate military targets. National armed-group context from a frontier department; not a Quindío finding.

tangentialFactors: The country's armed-group 'social cleansing' campaigns (Caquetá flyer pattern, 2024) name gays, lesbians and trans women alike, so LGB-wide hostility from non-state armed actors is part of the national climate a visitor moves through.
